exposure: General anesthesia (GA) vs. regional anesthesia (RA) for cesarean delivery
cohort: 356 very-low-birthweight infants delivered by cesarean section
finding: While GA in the absence of NRFS was associated with higher initial respiratory support needs, NRFS was a significant risk factor for adverse neonatal outcomes including low 5-minute Apgar score, increased respiratory support requirements, and pulmonary hypertension.
mod_finding: While general anesthesia was not independently associated with most adverse neonatal outcomes in very-low-birthweight infants, non-reassuring fetal status was associated with an increased risk of a low 5-minute Apgar score, increased respiratory support requirement, and pulmonary hypertension.
